records.issue_text: String#scrub requires Ruby >= 2.1 but this codebase supports Ruby 1.9, so even valid content raises NoMethodError
records.rationale: The new scheduled job `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` calls `i.content.scrub` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), but `String#scrub` is not available on Ruby 1.9. The repo’s Gemfile explicitly notes Ruby 1.9 support (e.g., “perftools only works on 1.9 atm”), so on such runtimes this line would raise `NoMethodError` and break feed polling even for valid content.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed_controller.rb renders 'loading' view that reloads the page after 30 seconds, but topic creation happens in an async Sidekiq job with no guarantee of completion, leaving an infinite reload loop on failure path
records.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and `render 'loading'`. The `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` view unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` after 30s. On each reload, if the Sidekiq job fails or never creates the `TopicEmbed` record, the controller will again see `topic_id` as nil, re-enqueue another `:retrieve_topic` job, re-render `loading`, and the page will keep reloading indefinitely (and can spam the queue). records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Referer is the sole embed authorization and is suppressed by modern browsers / private mode — `request.referer` is nil under no-referrer policies, causing `ensure_embeddable` to raise InvalidAccess and every embed view to return an error page in the iframe
records.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` authorizes embedding solely by checking `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when it doesn’t match. When `request.referer` is nil/blank (e.g., no-referrer policies), `URI('')` yields a nil host, which will not equal the configured host, so *all* embeds will error in the iframe even if `embed_url` is valid.

records.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring containment check, not an origin equality check, so any sender whose `e.origin` happens to be contained within `discourseUrl` will pass and can trigger `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` via a crafted `{type: 'discourse-resize', height: ...}` message. That is a verifiable security/correctness defect in the diff.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postMessage targetOrigin in embed.html.erb is taken from the client-controlled request.referer rendered into script, making the target origin attacker-influenced and causing resize postMessage to silently fail when mangled by escaping.
records.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the iframe posts a message using `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>');`. `request.referer` is client-controlled and typically a full URL including path/query, but `postMessage`’s `targetOrigin` must be an origin (scheme + host + optional port) like `https://example.com`, not a full referer URL. Passing a non-origin string can cause the message to be rejected or throw, breaking the resize behavior. Additionally, interpolating a header value into a JS string can be mangled by escaping/characters in the referer, further risking silent failure.

records.issue_text: [BUG] When the enqueued retrieve_topic job fails to produce an embed (embed_by_username unset, user doesn't exist, TopicRetriever#fetch_http silently returns nil), the controller returns the loading page which reloads every 30s forever — failure is invisible to the end user and no topic is ever created.
records.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and `render 'loading'`. The `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` view unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` after 30s. On each reload, if the Sidekiq job fails or never creates the `TopicEmbed` record, the controller will again see `topic_id` as nil, re-enqueue another `:retrieve_topic` job, re-render `loading`, and the page will keep reloading indefinitely (and can spam the queue). No retry/timeout/stop condition is present in the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import returns nil silently when url is not an http(s) URL (also reached from PollFeed when i.id isn't http), with no log or error result; feed entries with non-http ids are silently dropped with success reported.
records.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` will silently return `nil` for any non-HTTP(S) URL: `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, if `i.link` is blank or non-HTTP(S), it falls back to `url = i.id` without ensuring it is HTTP(S): `url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). That means feed items whose `id` is not an HTTP(S) URL will be passed to `TopicEmbed.import` and dropped with no log/error handling in the job, matching the finding’s mechanism.

records.issue_text: [BUG] SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no timeout, size cap, or error handling; errors inside the rss.items.each loop (e.g., item with no content element raising NoMethodError on nil.scrub, or PostCreator failure) abort all remaining items, and with retry: false the dropped entries are never retried.
records.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the job does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (around line 32). If a feed item has no `content` field, `i.content` will be nil and calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so such a failure would not be retried and would prevent that polling run from completing. The diff shows no nil-handling fallback (e.g., `i.description`).

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout and no read-size cap on a path invoked from the retrieve_topic job and disqus thor task; a slow or huge remote page hangs the job worker indefinitely, draining worker capacity.
records.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (no `open-uri` timeout options, no read-size cap). This method is invoked by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`) which is reached from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` worker (`TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`), and also by `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (`post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`). A slow/hung remote server or very large response can therefore block a job/thor run indefinitely, tying up worker capacity.
